value.name: present will witness details
value.description: Asha and Mr. Halloran discuss the will's witnessing, confirming the signatures and date.
evidence: "By Rosa Maldonado, the housekeeper, and a Mrs. Inez Carrasquillo, a neighbor on the block. Both signatures present. Dated February eleventh."

value.name: reveal will's equal thirds
value.description: Asha explains that the house is left in equal thirds to Daniel, Lucia, and Rosa, with a right of first refusal for any beneficiary who wants to stay.
evidence: "The house in equal thirds. Daniel, Lucia, Rosa. With a right of first refusal in favor of any beneficiary wishing to remain in residence, exercisable against the others at fair market value as established by independent appraisal."

value.name: report Daniel's reaction
value.description: Mr. Halloran asks how Daniel reacted, and Asha says Daniel asked her to stay for lunch.
evidence: "Christ have mercy," Mr. Halloran said, not unkindly. "How did Daniel take it."
"He asked me to stay for lunch."

value.name: decline Daniel's lunch invitation
value.description: Asha refuses Daniel's invitation to stay for lunch.

value.name: instruct filing of original will
value.description: Mr. Halloran tells Asha to bring in the original will so it can be lodged the next morning before the buyers' attorney wakes up.
evidence: "Bring the original in. We'll lodge it tomorrow morning before the buyers' attorney gets out of bed."

value.name: confirm will was photographed
value.description: Mr. Halloran asks whether the will was photographed, and Asha confirms Marcus took three angles and is making a working copy.
evidence: "Marcus did. Three angles. And he's making a working copy now."

value.name: assess housekeeper's reliability
value.description: Mr. Halloran asks about the housekeeper's reliability, and Asha vouches for her as the most reliable person in the house.
evidence: "And the witness — the housekeeper. She's reliable."
"She's the most reliable person in the house."

value.name: redefine housekeeper as client
value.description: Mr. Halloran tells Asha to treat the housekeeper as a client like the others, emphasizing her importance to the case.
evidence: "Then she's the most reliable person in the case," Mr. Halloran said, "and you should treat her as such, including by remembering that as of this afternoon she is your client to the same degree the other two are, which is to say not at all and entirely. You know what I mean."

value.name: ask about the older one
value.description: Mr. Halloran asks Asha how the older one is, prompting her to consider Daniel as she looks toward the dining room.
